title: Make target entity identity and money representation exact before product accounting slices

requirements.invariant: The backend-neutral target introduces executable typed domain values without importing Firebase or changing the released Firebase app or backend.

Every target Account, Client, Project, Item, Invoice, Transaction, Expense, Fee, Space, Attachment and Operation identity is a stable client-boundary text value generated independently of connectivity; the typed representation carries no Firestore path, Postgres sequence, Account-name or UI-order field and refuses path-shaped syntax.

Money is represented as signed integer minor units plus one explicit validated currency identity; construction, comparison and checked arithmetic never use floating point, infer a currency, silently convert currencies or overflow.

Domain primitives depend only on standard Swift and LedgerTargetCore types, carry no backend SDK, transport, database, dynamic payload, clock, random generator or global authentication state, and expose stable bounded failures.

The Swift boundary is compatible with later stable text IDs and bigint integer-minor-unit plus explicit-currency persistence, but this representation slice creates no table, migration, currency policy or persistence authority.

Exact-money and identity tests are deterministic, provider-free and cover valid boundaries, type separation, restart encoding, currency mismatch, arithmetic overflow and malformed decoded values rather than compile-only evidence.

items: CurrencyCode accepts exactly three uppercase ASCII letters and revalidates during decoding; it does not claim an ISO registry, locale, exchange-rate, default-currency or Account policy.

Money stores signed Int64 minor units and one CurrencyCode, offers zero, sign and structural value inspection, and permits numeric same-amount equality/order/add/subtract/negate only through explicit checked operations that reject currency mismatch and integer overflow.

ClientID, ProjectID, ItemID, InvoiceID, TransactionID, ExpenseID, FeeID, SpaceID and AttachmentID are distinct domain-identifier specializations that validate through the same bounded provider-free rules already used by AccountID, PrincipalID, EntityID and OperationID.
DomainPrimitiveFailure distinguishes malformed entity/currency/encoded money, currency mismatch and arithmetic overflow through stable bounded diagnostics without embedding raw values.

postgresSchema.notApplicable: This provider-free representation slice creates no Postgres table, column, check, foreign key, index, view or migration; later slices must map Money to bigint minor units plus explicit currency and IDs to stable text.

serverHandlers.notApplicable: No command payload, accounting sign rule, handler, transaction, lock, idempotency decision or server validation is implemented.

dataApiGrants.notApplicable: No relation, view or function is exposed through the Supabase Data API.

rlsPolicies.notApplicable: Opaque type safety is not authorization; no server rows or policies exist in this slice.

syncStreams.notApplicable: No PowerSync Stream, local table, upload shape, visibility policy or readiness rule is introduced.

items: Every identifier, CurrencyCode and Money value is immutable and Codable; decoding revalidates the same boundary so restart cannot admit whitespace, paths, oversized IDs, malformed currency or floating-point money.
Canonical sorted-key test encoding of representative and Int64-boundary values round-trips byte-identically without a clock, UUID, locale, database, network or global state.
Cross-currency comparison/arithmetic, addition/subtraction/negation overflow and malformed decoded values fail atomically with stable codes and no partial Money result.

storageMedia.notApplicable: AttachmentID is an opaque entity identity only; no bytes, path, URL, reference, upload, retention or deletion behavior exists.

appMcp.notApplicable: This slice defines reusable domain values only; it does not wire a form, formatter, query, command, MCP schema, transport or entry point.

migrationReconciliation.notApplicable: No source amount or identifier is transformed. Future migration slices must explicitly reconcile source units/currency/IDs rather than infer them through these types.

observabilityRunbooks.notApplicable: Stable local diagnostic codes are contract values only; no telemetry emission, metric, alert or runbook action is added.

items: The implementation remains inside the existing provider-free LedgerTargetCore and test targets and is not linked by changing either application project.
The slice cannot choose an Account currency, exchange/rounding/tax policy, amount sign or bounds, product lifecycle, schema, provider, feature activation, migration, deployment, release or cutover.

All current product formatting/calculation/model/app/MCP surfaces remain at their existing lifecycle status until owning vertical slices use the primitives and pass semantic parity/security/offline evidence.

verification.expected: Distinct stable typed IDs and exact Money/CurrencyCode values validate; same-currency equality, ordering and checked arithmetic produce exact Int64 results with no provider, locale or floating-point dependency.
Representative and Int64-boundary identifiers and Money values encode to deterministic integer/currency evidence and restore through the same validators with identical types and bytes.

Whitespace/path/oversized identifiers, lowercase/non-ASCII/wrong-length currency, fractional decoded money, cross-currency comparison/arithmetic, and every Int64 overflow edge fail atomically with stable safe codes.

verification.owner: pull-request CI Isolated target environment job
verification.expected: The exact implementation commit passes conversion traceability, provider/source-contamination and generated-contract checks, the complete target suite, both target builds and clean artifacts without changing an application project or claiming product, database, provider, migration or production behavior.

notes: Decision-independent Phase 1 technical foundation only. Signed integer representation permits later charges, credits and adjustments but does not authorize any product sign rule. Currency is a validated transport/domain identity, not an approved ISO list, Account default, exchange, locale, tax or rounding policy. The slice stops before product commands/read models, Postgres/PowerSync, app/MCP wiring, provider/hosted resources, migration, production access or cutover.
